title: SR2021 No8 2026 on-farm anaerobic-digestion installation QA controls

sources.title: SR2021 No 8: on-farm anaerobic digestion facility using farm wastes only, including use of the resultant biogas – installations

facts.source_fact: SR2021 No8 is an on-farm Part A anaerobic-digestion installation using farm wastes only.
The permit covers treatment capacity over 100 tonnes of waste or combined waste and non-waste per day.
The annual acceptance limit is no more than 100,000 tonnes.
The standard rules apply to England.
The rules do not allow vehicle fuelling stations.
Operations must comply with applicable BAT conclusions and BAT associated emission levels for waste treatment.
The rules include minimum sensitive-receptor distances linked to combustion-stack height.
The 26 February 2026 update changed biogas and biomethane treatment provisions.
The 2026 update added captured, treated and stored carbon dioxide requirements.
Routine venting of stored carbon dioxide is not allowed.
Emergency carbon dioxide venting must be designed, planned and managed for safety.
Storage of captured carbon dioxide is limited to 6 months prior to use.
CCR or HCR claims require a site-specific decarbonisation readiness report.
Point-source emissions are allowed only from listed sources and emission points.
Periodic monitoring is at least every 5 years for groundwater and 10 years for soil unless risk appraisal supports another basis.
Biogas combustion stacks are monitored annually over a minimum one-hour periodic reference period.
The listed NOx limit is 500 mg/m3 using EN 14792.
The listed carbon monoxide limit is 1400 mg/m3 using EN 15058.
The listed total VOC limit including methane is 1000 mg/m3 using EN 12619.
Permanent access must be provided where required to enable sampling and monitoring at emission points.

guard_patterns.handling: Preserve the cited farm-only permit fact.
Attach on-farm, farm-waste-only and installation scope.
Attach 26 February 2026 rule version and dated limits.
Carry point, frequency, method and standard provenance.
Do not infer parcel values from facility permit controls.
